title: A note in the rack
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Thursday. A note in the rack, folded, addressed to nobody: 'More of the boy at the counter.' There is no boy at the counter. Wood realizes the reader means Gully.

panels.composition: The laundromat. WOOD refilling the rack with the week's leftover copies. A folded note in the slot.

image.prompt: a young man refilling a wire rack with photocopied booklets and finding a folded note in the slot, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The note, open: a line in a careful old hand. 'More of the boy at the counter.'

image.prompt: close on a folded note in careful old-fashioned handwriting held in a young man's fingers, black and white, no words
image.notes: Letter after: 'More of the boy at the counter.'

image.prompt: a young man's face working something out, black and white, no words

panels.composition: Wood putting the note in his coat pocket, next to the misfold. Outside the window, small: the road to the boat launch.

image.prompt: a young man tucking a note into his coat pocket in a laundromat, a road to a boat launch visible through the window, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: The first request. It's for Gully. The note goes in the pocket with the misfold.
